# Every netlink.LinkAdd in pkg/ and the parent-interface gate that
# covers it (#571).
#
# WHAT THIS FILE IS FOR
#
# A parent NIC registers one rx_handler, so it is a macvlan port or an
# ipvlan port and never both. Any child link attached to a parent must
# therefore be serialised against every other operation on that parent,
# which is what Plugin.lockParent does. A LinkAdd that reaches a parent
# without holding that gate can be refused with "device or resource
# busy" — surfacing to a user as a failed `docker run` caused by an
# unrelated container.
#
# HOW THIS FILE AND THE COMPILER DIVIDE THE WORK
#
# The gate itself is proved by the type system, not here. lockParent
# returns a *parentGuard, addChildLink takes one, and nothing else
# constructs one — so a child link created through addChildLink is
# holding the gate as a matter of compilation, at every site, however
# many frames separate the lock from the LinkAdd.
#
# That leaves exactly one way to attach a child to a parent without the
# gate: call netlink.LinkAdd directly and bypass the helper. This file
# is the check on that path. scripts/check-parent-gate-accounting.sh
# matches every netlink.LinkAdd in pkg/ — the SUPERSET, however it is
# gated — and fails when a file is unlisted, when a count has changed,
# or when an entry has no justification. Bypassing the helper stays
# possible, because bridge networks legitimately need it, but it stops
# being something that can happen without anyone deciding it.
#
# So: the compiler answers "is the gate held on the guarded path", and
# this file answers "is anything off that path, and why". Neither
# question is answered by the other, which is why both exist.
#
# FORMAT
#
#   <path> <count>
#       <justification, indented, one or more lines>
#
# Entries are separated by blank lines. A bare path with no
# justification fails the gate: a list of paths with no reasons becomes
# a list somebody appends to. Same rule as .github/vuln-allowlist.txt.

pkg/plugin/parent_gate.go 1
    THE funnel. This is addChildLink, and it is the only place in the
    plugin that attaches a child link to a parent NIC. It takes a
    *parentGuard it never reads: the parameter exists so the caller
    cannot reach this line without having gone through lockParent, which
    is what makes the requirement a compile error rather than a review
    comment.
    Every parent-attached site in the plugin — the endpoint's own child
    in parent_attached.go, the reclaim's temporary link in
    orphan_release.go, the validate_dhcp preflight probe in
    dhcp_probe.go — reaches the kernel through here.

pkg/plugin/orphan_release.go 1
    The bridge-mode branch of releaseLink: a veth pair for handing back
    an orphaned lease on a bridge network. NOT parent-attached — a
    bridge network has no parent NIC, nothing registers an rx_handler,
    and there is no parent to contend for. Correctly ungated.
    The macvlan/ipvlan branch of the same function is the one that IS
    parent-attached, and it goes through addChildLink.
    A note for whoever reads the reclaim next, because it is the thing
    most likely to be "tidied": the gate for that branch is taken in
    synthesiseRelease, several frames up, and it has to stay there. The
    hold must span the entire reclaim — the DHCP round trip AND the
    deferred LinkDel — because the parent stays occupied until the child
    link is gone, not merely until the DHCPRELEASE is sent. Moving it
    down to sit lexically around the LinkAdd looks like an improvement
    and restores the exact bug the gate was added for: an ipvlan reclaim
    link left on the parent while a macvlan endpoint is created, which
    is EBUSY on an operation the user did not cause.

pkg/plugin/network.go 1
    The bridge-mode veth pair created at CreateEndpoint. Same reasoning
    as the bridge branch above: no parent NIC, nothing to serialise
    against, and adding a gate here would serialise bridge endpoints
    against nothing.
